newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley skipped bonuses in 1996.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley skipped bonuses in 1996.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co omitted annual performance bonuses for its key senior managers in 1996, the printing company said in a proxy for its March 27 annual shareholders meeting.
A spokesman said the company failed to reach certain internal economic value-added measures. Specific targets were not disclosed.
R.R. Donnelley last year posted a loss of $157.6 million, or $1.04 per share, after a $435 million restructuring charge.

John Walter, the company's former chairman and chief executive, was among those who received no bonuses. Walter, who left Donnelley on October 22 to become president of AT&T Corp, was paid a salary of $986,790, including vacation pay.
Walter's base salary was not increased in 1996, the proxy said.

"Walter did not receive an annual incentive compensation payout under the annual plan for 1996," the proxy noted. "Walter, like other executive officers, did not receive a payout in 1996 under any long-term award, as no such awards vested in 1996."
R.R. Donnelley spokesman William Lowe said the company's actions are designed to align management's interests with those of the shareholders.
